answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only after each identity completes a costly, repeatable task: for example, escrow a stake, fulfill a randomly assigned job, and let the buyer attest to delivery before the stake unlocks. The atlas of completed jobs becomes a trust signal, while a kernel of validators checks signatures and prevents one payment from being counted twice. A sybil attacker must fund and operate many identities, risking real capital on each; identities alone cannot cheaply manufacture successful history.
